paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter. Everybody is working hard to get Absalom home, and nobody is doing the one thing that matters. Joab builds a whole stage play, the woman from Tekoa delivers the lines, and Absalom gets back to Jerusalem. But the king says, "He may return to his house, but he must not see my face." (2 Samuel 14:24) Being back in the city and being back with his father are two different things.

The woman's words carry the heart of it. She says, "Yet God does not take away a life, but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him." (2 Samuel 14:14) That is the lesson. God is not looking for ways to keep people out. He is working on ways to bring them in. I spent years shoved in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you it's something else to find out somebody was working on the way back for me.

Now, this chapter also shows how hard it is to fix a broken relationship halfway. Two years pass, Absalom burns a field to get attention, and a kiss finally comes. I think that kiss is good, but I also think it's not the whole story. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is not over. Today, ask yourself who is waiting on you to close the distance, and who you are keeping at arm's length.
